messages:
Amy: Preflight note — I'm scheduling a terraform apply for release-2026.02 network changes in the 23:00-01:00 UTC change window. This touches transit peering, route-table fine-grains, and a small NAT tweak. Requesting watchers and a rollback owner.
Ben: Ack — I'll watch peering/BGP and NAT behavior. What provider version are we using? Last time we hit drift with a bump.
Carlos: We kept the provider pinned in the module root to `hashicorp/aws 4.50.0`. No provider upgrade in this run. I also added a `canary` flag to only flip a portion of routes initially.
InfraLead: Sounds good. Please run the apply serially for the peering steps. Suggest `-parallelism=2` for safety. Deploy-bot, can you take the serial apply and annotate the release notes metadata?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled apply in 20m, mode=serial, apply_lock=true. Plan is available: https://deploy.logs/redwood/1777770001/plan.txt :robot_face:
Amy: Plan looks clean on my pass. Rollback plan: restore previous RT entries + revert canary by setting `canary=false` and re-running apply; if propagation stuck we may `terraform state rm` for the problematic resource and re-import. Ben, will you own immediate rollback?
Ben: :thumbsup: I'll own rollback. Runbook summary I'll use: 1) flip canary off 2) revert route entries 3) if route leak persists, revert peering change and open a support ticket with the cloud provider. I'll post exact `aws` cli snippets here pre-apply.
SRE Oncall: I'll monitor infra and app-level metrics. If p95 latency > 150ms or error-rate >= 1% sustained for 15m, we escalate and trigger rollback checklist.
Carlos: Release notes drafted: "network: transit peering optimization + more-granular route-table scopes (release-2026.02)". Tagging the release and adding the changelog link to the plan.
Amy: Quick pre-apply checklist: 1) provider pin verified 2) state snapshot uploaded to S3 (`s3://tf-state/prod-2026-02.bak`) 3) deploy-bot dry-run passed 4) oncall acked. Please confirm each.
InfraLead: Backup snapshot complete and hash verified.
Ben: Acknowledged, I'm standing by.
SRE Oncall: Acked — watching dashboards.
Amy: Kicking apply now. I'll post outputs as they come.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: apply started by Amy. Logs: https://deploy.logs/redwood/1777770001/apply.log. Will update with result. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(deploy-bot posts intermediate)
deploy-bot: apply step 3/7 completed — peering attachments created, route propagation in progress. No errors so far.
Ben: Seeing route entries on our monitoring side, propagation looks to be ~30s per route. Continuing to watch NAT behavior.
SRE Oncall: No app-side spikes yet. Latency stable.
(deploy-bot final)
deploy-bot: apply succeeded. All resources applied and state updated. Canary enabled at 10% traffic for 30m observation. No rollback required. Summary: small route-table scope tightened, peering optimized. Changelog entry posted to the release notes. :white_check_mark:
Amy: Thanks everyone — leaving this thread open for the 30m canary window, but from my side this is a successful rollout. If anything odd shows up, call the rollback runbook.
